Fen.narrative: I mend what the sea, cold, and careless hands break. Most households owe me something, though I would rather they came before a wound turns bad. I believe the Oath matters because I have sewn up people from both towns.
goals: Keep my patients alive through the next hard season
Keep peace between Saltreach and Brandholm
Make time for my family despite the calls for help
Fen.mood: Thoughtful and watchful, with old grief close to the surface.

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: partner
relations.note: She carries more than her share and still finds a kind word for me.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: I want her to have room to be a child, not another pair of hands.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: sister
relations.note: We learned to tend people together, though she has made her own home between the towns.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She listens before judging, and I trust her to hear both sides.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: ally
relations.note: Her records can prevent a quarrel from becoming a wound.

relations.name: Corin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He was Tomas's fishing partner and remembers him with warmth.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: I understand her grief, but I cannot make certainty out of what I saw.

relations.name: Tomas
relations.label: memory
relations.note: I treated his body and have never forgotten the wound I found.

memories.gist: When I treated Tomas's body after he came back from the forest, I saw a wound I have never spoken of. I have carried that silence ever since.
Rose and I once spent a night tending a fever in a drafty house; we took turns at the fire and neither of us slept much.
Old Aud sat with me after a difficult treatment and reminded me that a steady hand matters more than a loud certainty.
Oriel came home smelling of smoke from the racks and made Kit laugh before I had even washed the day's herbs from my hands.

stances.why: I have tended people from both towns; their injuries do not care which side of the stone they came from.
I know what I saw when Tomas was brought home, and I know what I did not see.
A debt can be settled later; a worsening wound may not wait.

Fen.secret: When I treated Tomas's body, I saw a wound I never spoke of. I have told no one what I made of it.

Oriel.narrative: I work the Smokehouse racks for Bea, and I know how smoke, time, and a careful fire can save a catch. The pay comes in marks and fish, as agreed, but hired hands still have to ask others to speak for us. At home, I want Fen and Kit to have something warm to come back to.
goals: Earn enough in marks and fish to keep our household secure
Be treated fairly for the work I do at the Smokehouse
Keep Kit safe and give her room to explore
Oriel.mood: Practical, affectionate, and a little tired.

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: partner
relations.note: He gives so much of himself to other people that I remind him to come home.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She brings home stones as if each one has a story.

relations.name: Bea
relations.label: employer
relations.note: She pays what she promised, and I can see she is carrying a heavy load.

relations.name: Lark
relations.label: coworker
relations.note: She can turn a sour shift into a laugh, and she does not forget what hands are owed.

relations.name: Cade
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He speaks calmly about giving hired hands a voice, and I think he means it.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: Tally-keeper
relations.note: I want the Tally to count the work we do as clearly as it counts what we owe.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: brother-in-law
relations.note: His shouting makes a hard day harder, even when I understand his anger.

relations.name: Nell
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is patient company, and she knows what it is to worry over family.

memories.gist: Bea paid me in marks and fish at the market as agreed, even after a hard week at the racks. I went home feeling that a promise kept matters.
Lark and I worked the smoking racks side by side while the wind kept pushing smoke back into our faces; she made me laugh when I was ready to quit.
Kit came home proudly carrying a smooth odd stone, and Fen made time to hear where she had found it.

stances.why: We do essential work and should have a say in the decisions that shape our lives.
Marks and fish are how I make sure my family has what it needs.
Peace between the towns matters to anyone who depends on steady trade.

Kit.narrative: I like the little shells by the water and the odd stones I find on the paths. At home, Fen smells of herbs and Oriel smells of smoke. I like when they listen to what I found.
goals: Show my finds to Fen and Oriel

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: father
relations.note: He knows about herbs and always listens when I tell him what I found.

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She makes our home feel warm, even when she smells like the Smokehouse.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: I like hearing about the things he sees near the stone.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: We are little enough to play together without worrying about the towns.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She is my father's sister and she knows how to help people feel better.

memories.gist: I found a strange smooth stone and brought it home to show my parents. They both listened to where I found it.
